title: Getting involved with the Dixie Cups through Joe Jones
summary: Joe Jones brought the Dixie Cups to him, and they went to New York where Jones talked his way into a Leiber and Stoller studio session, getting the group signed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I wondered, uh, in the middle of all this, didn't you, didn't you do some work with the Dixie Cups? Oh!
Gee, missed. I think we missed that.
I have it on my list. We missed all of that.

How'd you get involved with the Dixie Cups? Uh, Dixie Cups, uh, and they had my band, and, uh, Joe Jones heard the band, and he came by and said if I would do some things with him. You know, he had a couple of artists that he wanted to record if I would help him with it. Uh-huh. One of the artists was, uh, was the Dixie Cups. There was Al Robinson. And I think at that time, uh, uh, what is this boy named that did work, that's Fass Domino's, uh, brother-in-law. Uh, he did a, did something. And we all went to, uh, uh, we all went to, uh, Motown. Uh, no. We went to New York, uh, with these artists that Joe, you know, paid, paid away and all that kind of stuff. And he tried to leave some things to some, and we tried to get some, uh, people to listen at the Dixie Cups, you know. So one day, we all went to a studio with, uh, with Joe. And we, Joe learned that they had a session going on, uh, for Lieber and Stoll, uh, some group or something like that. And they, and, and, and, uh, Joe got there before the, this group came in and do their stuff. And the musicians, I mean, not the musicians, the studio thought that was for Lieber and Stoller. I don't know if Joe told him that, I imagine. So, so when Lieber and Stoller came in, uh, uh, he saw the band set up. And he, he told the people, and he said, I thought this was our studio time. And Joe Jones went up there and said, well, I would like for you to hear, uh, hear something, you know. And the first thing he did was he let the, uh, he let them hear the Dixie Cups. And right then and there, they took, they took, uh, because of the nerve of Joe, they took the group and, and history was made from then on. But that's how they got recorded. But Joe came up to me, and the Dixie Cups was very, very young. And they had this natural thing that they can hear their own harmony. You know, the three girls. And, and, and, uh, it was very easy to work with them. They was raw. They had to, you know, put the, put some edges on them. But they, uh, they had natural talent. They still do. Uh, and that's how I ain't got, that's how I got involved with them. You know, I did some work, uh, raw work with them and all of that.
